guidance: If the machine reading runs lines together differently from the print, or puts a few words at the edge of the box in another order, pick Yes, nothing missing.
If the machine reading has all the text in the box and more besides (words from the next column), pick Yes, nothing missing.
If the box holds no text at all (a picture, an ornament, a divider line or blank paper), pick Not text. A headline or an advertisement is text.
intro: Each block of print comes from an English-language page in Chronicling America, the Library of Congress's collection of historic American newspapers. A program read the page. We want to know whether it missed any of the print.
name: English: missing text
question: Does the machine reading include every line printed in the box? Ignore wrong letters and a word or two cut off at the edge of the box.
rules: The box on the page marks a block of print. Below the page is that block enlarged, then the machine reading of the same place. Wrong letters don't matter. Pick No if a line or more of the print in the box (a line, a passage, a column) is missing from the machine reading, even if the rest is perfect.
title: English newspapers: missing text
